title: 429 Too Many Requests - HTTP status reference
content: The HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response status code indicates the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time (rate limiting). It was defined in RFC 6585. A Retry-After header might be included in this response indicating how long to wait before making a new request. The Retry-After value can be either a number of seconds (delay-seconds) or an HTTP-date after which to retry. Clients should honour Retry-After rather than retrying immediately. Servers may also use 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After for maintenance.

title: Exponential Backoff and Jitter: why your retries need randomness
content: When many clients retry failed requests at the same time, plain exponential backoff still creates synchronized waves of traffic. Adding jitter spreads retries out. The 'full jitter' strategy picks the sleep time uniformly at random between 0 and min(cap, base * 2 ** attempt). For example with base = 0.5 seconds and cap = 30 seconds, attempt 3 sleeps between 0 and 4 seconds. Full jitter reduces total work and completion time compared with no jitter or equal jitter. Always cap the number of attempts and prefer a server-provided Retry-After value when present.

title: Retrying HTTP requests in Python with tenacity and requests
content: Python example of retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Install tenacity, then: from tenacity import retry, stop_after_attempt, wait_random_exponential, retry_if_exception_type. Decorate your function with @retry(wait=wait_random_exponential(multiplier=0.5, max=30), stop=stop_after_attempt(6), retry=retry_if_exception_type(RateLimited)). Inside the function call requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=10); if response.status_code == 429, read int(response.headers.get('Retry-After', '1')), sleep for that many seconds, and raise RateLimited so tenacity schedules another attempt. Alternatively urllib3's Retry(total=5, backoff_factor=0.5, status_forcelist=[429, 500, 502, 503], respect_retry_after_header=True) mounted on a requests Session through HTTPAdapter honours Retry-After automatically.

title: What is a pending authorization on my card statement?
content: Merchants often place a temporary authorization hold to confirm a card is valid. The hold shows as pending and reduces your available balance but is not a completed charge. Most holds drop off within 1 to 7 business days depending on your card issuer. If you see a pending item and a posted charge for the same amount, usually only the posted charge will remain. Contact your bank if a hold remains after 7 business days.

title: Excluding SaaS applications from TLS inspection on corporate proxies
content: Many corporate web proxies decrypt HTTPS traffic (TLS inspection, also called SSL decryption or SSL bumping) by re-signing certificates with a corporate root CA. Desktop applications that use certificate pinning reject these re-signed certificates and fail to connect. The usual fix is to add the application's domains to the proxy's TLS-inspection bypass (do-not-decrypt) list, while still allowing them through the firewall on port 443. Most proxy consoles have a 'SSL inspection exemptions' or 'bypass list' setting that accepts wildcard domains such as *.vendor.example. Changes typically take a few minutes to propagate to clients.

title: How to enable long path support (paths longer than 260 characters) in Windows 10 and 11
content: Windows historically limits paths to 260 characters (MAX_PATH). On Windows 10 version 1607 and later, and Windows 11, you can remove this limit for applications that opt in. Option 1, Group Policy: open gpedit.msc, go to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Filesystem and enable 'Enable Win32 long paths'. Option 2, Registry: set the DWORD value LongPathsEnabled to 1 under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem. Administrator rights are required, and a restart (or at least signing out) is recommended. Applications must also declare long path awareness in their manifest.

title: What is SAML single sign-on and how do I connect an identity provider?
content: SAML 2.0 single sign-on lets users authenticate with a central identity provider (IdP) such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or Google Workspace instead of separate passwords. Setup usually involves creating a SAML application in the IdP, entering the service provider's ACS URL and Entity ID, then uploading the IdP metadata XML or certificate to the service provider. Many SaaS vendors only include SSO in higher-priced tiers.

title: GDPR Article 17: the right to erasure explained
content: Article 17 of the GDPR gives individuals the right to have personal data erased without undue delay in certain circumstances, for example when the data is no longer necessary or consent is withdrawn. Controllers must generally respond within one month of the request, extendable by two further months for complex requests.

title: CloudBox review 2026: is it worth it?
content: CloudBox is a solid file storage platform with a good API. Pricing starts at $15 per month.
